Definition: from G444 and κτείνω (to kill); a manslayer:--murderer. Compare G5406.
BiblicalUsage: John says no murderer has eternal life abiding in him, and that the devil was a murderer from the beginning. The word is the plain name for a man-killer, and John ties it to hatred: whoever hates his brother is a murderer.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for a murderer holds no doctrine of its own; its terror is John's, that hatred is murder in the heart before it is murder with the hands.
